stem: A company has 1,200 employees. The dot plot shows the one-way commuting distance, in kilometers, for each of 25 employees selected at random. Based on the sample, which of the following is the best estimate of the number of the company's employees whose one-way commuting distance is more than 10 kilometers?
solution: In the sample, 9 employees have distances greater than 10 kilometers (11, 12, 12, 13, 14, 15, 17, 18 and 22).

explanation.A: Incorrect. 9 is the number of SAMPLED employees who commute more than 10 kilometers; it has not been scaled up to 1,200 employees.
explanation.B: Incorrect. This is the estimate for employees who commute 10 kilometers or LESS: \(\frac{16}{25}(1{,}200)\).
explanation.C: Incorrect. This counts the two employees who commute exactly 10 kilometers, giving \(\frac{11}{25}(1{,}200)\); exactly 10 is not MORE than 10.
explanation.D: Correct. 9 of the 25 sampled employees (36%) commute more than 10 kilometers, and \(0.36(1{,}200) = 432\).

verify:
choices = {o: choices[n] for o, n in {'C': 'A', 'D': 'B', 'B': 'C', 'A': 'D'}.items()}; answer = {'A': 'C', 'B': 'D', 'C': 'B', 'D': 'A'}[answer]  # shuffled: original letters
v = figure['values']
assert len(v) == 25
k9 = len([d for d in v if d > 10])
est = Rational(k9, 25) * 1200
assert est == 432 and value(choices[answer]) == est
assert all(value(choices[k]) != est for k in choices if k != answer)
